steps.say: Most gallstones sit quietly for life and need nothing done. Pain after fatty food that grips the right ribs, with fever and a tender catch on pressing beneath them, means the gallbladder wall is inflamed.
steps.tx: Asymptomatic stones carry under **2 percent** (two percent) yearly biliary pain risk and need no treatment, while **biliary colic** (fatty-food right-rib pain) with **wall thickening** (swollen gallbladder wall) over **3 mm** (three millimetres) and **Murphy sign** (caught breath on pressure) marks acute cholecystitis.

vis.alt: Outline of the gallbladder and bile ducts showing cholesterol and pigment stones with a duct stone.
vis.caption: Gallstone locations and types: cholesterol and pigment stones in the gallbladder with a common duct stone below. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Inflammation is graded from mild to organ-threatening, and the grade sets the clock. Mild disease goes to theatre within days, while failing kidneys or lungs demand drainage first and surgery later.
steps.tx: **Tokyo grading** (cholecystitis severity scale) spans mild localised disease through moderate with palpable mass or symptoms over **72 hours** (three days) to severe with **organ dysfunction** (failing kidneys or lungs), deciding between early surgery and drainage in each admitted patient.

steps.say: Removing an inflamed gallbladder early is safer than waiting for it to cool. Before any vessel is clipped, the surgeon clears the triangle until only two structures enter the gallbladder and nothing else.
steps.tx: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within **72 hours** (three days) of onset beats delayed surgery, with the **critical view of safety** (cleared triangle view) exposing **2 structures** (two structures) entering the gallbladder, verified on the clear liver bed view before any clip is applied.

vis.alt: Operative view of an inflamed gallbladder with the cystic artery and duct isolated in the cleared triangle.
vis.caption: Critical view of safety: cystic artery and duct isolated with the cystic plate cleared before clipping. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Stones that escape into the main duct bring jaundice and shaking chills. Small ones are fished out through the mouth scope first, while the surgeon clears big ones directly during the gallbladder operation.
steps.tx: Common duct stones with cholangitis, jaundice or dilated duct over **6 mm** (six millimetres) need preoperative **ERCP clearance** (scope stone fishing), while single-stage laparoscopic **bile duct exploration** (direct duct stone removal) suits fit patients with large stones and a roomy duct.

steps.say: A stone wedged in the neck can squash the neighbouring main duct from outside, mimicking cancer with yellow eyes and itching. Small dents are repaired simply, but a hole between the ducts needs a new join to bowel.
steps.tx: **Mirizzi** (neck-stone duct squeeze) compresses the common hepatic duct from an impacted cystic duct stone, graded Csendes **I to V** (one to five) up to **cholecystobiliary fistula** (duct-to-duct hole) needing hepaticojejunostomy rather than simple removal of the gallbladder alone in these patients.

rows: Partial wall loss, repair over tube

steps.say: A giant stone can erode straight into the bowel and lodge at the stomach outlet, blocking all food. The stone is lifted out through the bowel wall first, and the gallbladder waits for another day.
steps.tx: **Bouveret** (outlet-blocking gallstone) with gastric outlet obstruction from a large fistula stone over **2.5 cm** (two and a half centimetres) needs **enterolithotomy** (bowel stone removal) first, with cholecystectomy deferred to a second stage once inflammation settles fully and the patient regains strength.

steps.say: Growths on the gallbladder wall are judged by size and shape. Small floating ones are watched with sound scans, while big flat ones or any in a scarred duct disease need the organ out.
steps.tx: Gallbladder polyps over **10 mm** (ten millimetres), **sessile** (flat-based) shape or sclerosing cholangitis background need cholecystectomy for malignant potential, while small mobile polyps suit ultrasound surveillance at intervals with size tracking on every visit for early change detection over time.

steps.say: Patients too sick for an operation get a drain through the skin into the angry gallbladder. Pus pours out, fever settles, and weeks later when strength returns the gallbladder is removed properly.
steps.tx: Percutaneous **cholecystostomy** (skin drain into gallbladder) bridges severe cholecystitis in unfit patients, with **interval cholecystectomy** (planned later removal) at **6 to 8 weeks** (six to eight weeks) once sepsis resolves fully and fitness improves enough for safe anaesthesia and quick recovery.
